newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks eke out modest gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks eke out modest gains by close.

text.p: The Australian share market eked out some modest gains after a patchy performance by the close on Wednesday with only minimal interest shown by investors.
The All Ordinaries index added 8.8 points to 2,646.4.

Turnover struggled to top the A$500 million mark, a clear indication of the abject lack of investor interest, with brokers saying offshore traders were turned away by concerns over the rapidly declining Australian dollar.
"Volumes were slight, probably because of the Australian dollar. It is always a big factor in overseas traders' minds," said a Sydney-based broker.
Trade was mixed with a short term view reflected in the choppy trading conditions.
"It was all over the place. BHP ran hard then fell away and the banks were a bit mixed," the broker said.

Bellwether BHP ended down eight at A$18.19 (US$13.28) in volatile trade, while among banks, Commonwealth Bank added 17 cents to A$16.33, while Westpac Banking Corp made most ground, up 13 cents to A$7.80.
"Some people may be more confident on the Bank of Melbourne (bid) but it was probably more just trading factors on the day," the broker said.

The market is waiting for the Australian Competition and Consumer Commision's ruling on Westpac's A$9.75 a share bid for the Victorian-based Bank of Melbourne. Bank of Melbourne shares closed 3.5 cents higher at A$9.43.

In the recently beleaguered gold sector, takeover speculation around Joseph Gutnick-controlled Great Central Mines Ltd stole the show as rumours did the rounds of a possible bid from giant Canadian gold miner Barrick Gold.
Great Central shares jumped 10 percent to A$2.71 by the close, although the company denied a bid was on the table or that it was aware of any such bid.
"The talk is in the market. It is probably a 50/50 bet," said Peter Morgan, Australian equities manager at Perpetual Funds Management.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
